item.title: Florida State interim coach Rick Stockstill leads Seminoles to win in debut, ends road losing streak
item.description: Amari Thomas scored the go-ahead touchdown with 2:29 left as Florida State rallied from a 17-7 deficit to beat Boston College in Rick Stockstill's debut.
item.content:encoded:
Florida State opened the Rick Stockstill era with a road win Saturday. Those victories have been hard to come by for the Seminoles in recent years.

FSU defeated Boston College 31-24 behind two rushing touchdowns from Amari Thomas. His 11-yard score late in the fourth quarter put the Seminoles ahead and made Stockstill a winner in his first game as interim coach. Entering Saturday, FSU had not won a game away from Doak Campbell Stadium since Nov. 25, 2023. Ashton Daniels completed 15 of 26 passes for 178 yards and an interception.

Boston College quarterback Mason McKenzie finished the day with 166 passing yards, two touchdowns and an interception.

ARCH MANNING, TEXAS ESCAPE MISSOURI AFTER WILD OFFICIATING CONTROVERSY SENDS SEC SHOWDOWN INTO CHAOS

With it tied at 24-all, the Seminoles marched 90 yards in 14 plays, with Thomas breaking to the outside for the go-ahead score with 2:29 left.

"This was emotional for me today," said a teary-eyed Stockstill, who was one of legendary FSU coach Bobby Bowden’s first quarterbacks. "I guess I wanted it as much for our players in there as I did for my former teammates and all our other players that came before us. It was special, it’s emotional.

FLORIDA STATE FIRES AD MICHAEL ALFORD, AS MIKE NORVELL’S SEAT REACHES A BOILING POINT IN TALLAHASSEE

"I poured my heart and soul into this place as a player, and I was going to do that for these next couple of months here," he said.

McKenzie was shaken up and left midway into the third quarter, but returned the next series and capped off a crazy trick play when everyone on offense spun around in a circle before they lined up in a spread formation, snapped it and he tossed an underhanded pass for a two-yard touchdown to Javarius Green that pushed BC ahead 24-21.

"It was just a play in our game plan that we thought would be good for these guys," BC coach Bill O’Brien said.

Gabe Panikowski’s 22-yard field goal tied it.

Playing its first game since firing coach Mike Norvell after six-plus seasons, Florida State erased a 17-7 second-quarter deficit by putting up two touchdowns in the final six minutes of the half. Thomas’ 20-yard run down the right sideline sliced the gap to three points.

The Eagles entered Saturday’s game looking to rebound from one of the most lopsided losses of O’Brien’s tenure. Boston College lost that game 47-2. The Eagles will travel to Indiana next week to face No. 11 Notre Dame.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

item.title: Alabama finally puts it all together, dominates LSU and leaves Lane Kiffin staring at $40 million CFP disaster
item.description: Lane Kiffin fell to 0-6 against Alabama as head coach after the Crimson Tide defense held LSU to one touchdown on four red zone possessions.
item.content:encoded:
Alabama spent the past five days taking heat from across the country over its No. 5 ranking in the initial College Football Playoff poll released Tuesday.

On Saturday, Kalen DeBoer’s Crimson Tide took out its frustration on Lane Kiffin and LSU in front of a stunned crowd in Baton Rouge, delivering a result that could have major ramifications for the Tigers’ playoff hopes.

We all spent the past week arguing over why the Tide would be ranked eight spots ahead of No. 13 Tennessee after the Vols won the head-to-head matchup last month in Knoxville.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF RANKINGS: MIAMI TAKES TOP SPOT, INDIANA CRACKS TOP FIVE IN FIRST OFFICIAL RELEASE

The nonstop chatter around Alabama struggling to find an identity behind head coach Kalen DeBoer had become a hot-button topic around college football, while LSU fans were under the impression that Lane Kiffin was turning a corner in the Bayou.

Boy, how quickly the tables have turned.

LSU spent more than $40 million building its roster this season, acquiring a group of stars through the transfer portal. Now, the Tigers enter the second weekend of November with three losses and their CFP hopes hanging by a thread.

On the other side of the field, not worried about Kevin Costner or other celebrities making the walk into a game alongside the head coach, Kalen Deboer has now finally pieced it all together for a squad that has the talent to compete for a national championship.

This is the Alabama team the CFP committee thought should be ranked 5th in the country, and the Tide backed up their thinking in a dominant second half way in Baton Rouge.

Maybe it was the return of Ryan Coleman-Williams or multiple starters on both sides of the ball, but Alabama finally looked like the type of team we thought would grace our television screens on a weekly basis without the hiccups.

In front of over 100,000 fans inside Tiger Stadium, it was Alabama's Keelon Russell who fully came out of his shell in what will turn out to be a massive game in terms of his team making the playoff.

Three touchdowns and over 200 yards passing, offensive coordinator Ryan Grubb provided his freshman quarterback with the ammunition needed to put Alabama in a spot to win this game.

But, winning 31-13 in "Death Valley"?

LANE KIFFIN FUMES OVER ALABAMA KICKOFF TIME, ACCUSES SEC OF NOT WANTING LSU TO WIN

That's a massive slice of humble-pie served up to Lane Kiffin, and the ones that doubted the heart of this Alabama football team, by a Crimson Tide defense that held LSU to just one touchdown on four redzone possessions.

Sure, LSU was moving the ball on offense, but that did not translate to points in Alabama's bend but don't break mindset that had Lane Kiffin shrugging his arms in frustration along the sidelines throughout the third and fourth quarter.

On the other hand, Alabama scoring 21 unanswered points put the final nail in this LSU football team that will host a much better looking Texas Longhorns squad next week in Baton Rouge.

Sure, the Tigers could upset Steve Sarkisian's football team, but there was nothing from the LSU offense that should give fans hope that they can hold up against a Texas defense that will get even healthier over the next week.

Obviously, this is the type of scenario that LSU fans were not expecting. The noise that comes with Lane Kiffin is just that — noise. Yes, the Tigers were good enough to have us all wondering how this game would turn out during the third quarter.

Fifteen minutes later, Kiffin's record against Alabama as a head coach was 0-6.

Olivia Dunne and Paul Skenes walking with Lane Kiffin through the Tiger Walk makes for some fantastic social media content. But following that up by getting beaten in the trenches by an Alabama team that has been dissected all week for its flaws will not go over well in Baton Rouge.

A massive statement was made by Alabama on Saturday night during a week in which the entire country questioned just how good they actually were.

Now, everyone should be worried about what this Kalen DeBoer team can do over the next few weeks leading up to selection Sunday in the college football playoff.

item.title: Tim McGraw warns of ‘most dangerous’ times in marriage after 30 years with Faith Hill
item.description: Tim McGraw reveals the "most dangerous parts" of a long marriage and why rediscovering Faith Hill during their toughest moments matters most.
item.content:encoded:
Tim McGraw shared his insight into what the "most difficult" part of marriage is, after being married for 30 years.

During a recent interview with Esquire’s "What I’ve Learned," the 59-year-old country star shared that as his three children with Faith Hill grow up and start their own lives, the two of them find themselves "stepping into a new phase of life."

"Sometimes that requires not talking about it and just moving on through," he said. "And sometimes it requires sitting down and talking about it a little bit, saying, 'Hey, we need to check in a little bit and see where we're at now that everything's changing.'"

He went on to say that "points of change in a marriage" can come "regularly throughout a long marriage," and these can often be "the most dangerous parts, I think, for a marriage."

GREAT RELATIONSHIPS HAVE 3 ESSENTIAL INGREDIENTS — AND ONE FACTOR THAT CAN RUIN EVERYTHING

"And not talking about things and not clearing the air and not sort of rediscovering each other at every chance you get," he said. "I think the best time to dive into each other and really rediscover each other at the worst times when you think things are falling apart."

In his opinion, it is important to have a strong foundation and "to always go back to it," because "the longer you wait to go back to it," there may come a time where it becomes "unreachable, and you never can cross that divide."

McGraw and Hill tied the knot in October 1996 and have been a country music power couple ever since. Over the course of their marriage, they have welcomed three daughters together; Gracie, 29, Maggie, 28, and Audrey, 24.

They have also recorded multiple duets together during their relationship, including "It's Your Life," the Grammy Award-winning "Let's Make Love" and "Speak to a Girl," which was featured on their first-ever collaborative album, "The Rest of Our Life."

In an Instagram post shared on their 30th anniversary, McGraw looked back on their wedding day, writing that as he stood in his aunt's backyard he "watched my future walk towards me" and "In front of our closest family and friends, I was bound to the most beautiful soul."

"A lady that was glowing in my eyes, expanding my heart, and giving me all the love she had. I was and still am bewildered by her capacity to love, forgive, nurture and be full of joy and laughter," he wrote. "She is a gift to the world for sure, however, for us, we get Her, all of her. And I (and my girls) know who is ours, completely. It’s difficult to describe what she means, she is the center of gravity to my life and our girls lives and anyone who knows Audrey Faith McGraw."

The post was accompanied by a slideshow of the two of them over the years, including videos of them on stage together.

Although the two have been married for three decades and have collaborated musically a few times, McGraw shared in November 2023 that some of their biggest disagreements are about their music.

"I mean we're two different artists. We don't always agree, musically. In fact, some of our biggest disagreements come when we're putting a tour together," McGraw admitted during Time Magazine's "Person of the Week" podcast.

"Faith's very type-A," he added. "I'm a mess. I'll throw clothes everywhere. I mean she's always, constantly on me about picking my clothes up. I mean, I spent 30 years living in a hotel… In and out. So I'm just constantly throwing stuff everywhere and she's like, ‘You got to clean up after yourself.’"

item.title: Bridget Fonda spotted in rare LA outing 24 years after her final on-screen appearance
item.description: Bridget Fonda was spotted out in Los Angeles 24 years after her last on-screen role, having previously told paparazzi she has no plans to return to acting.
item.content:encoded:
Bridget Fonda stepped out for a rare public outing in Los Angeles, 24 years after she last appeared on-screen.

The 62-year-old actress was photographed while out to lunch on Monday, Nov. 2, keeping it casual in black sweatpants and a white tank top, paired with a yellow collared button-up shirt.

She accessorized the look with a black crossbody bag and sunglasses, and styled her hair in a ponytail.

As the granddaughter of Academy Award-winning actor, Henry Fonda, known for his roles in "The Grapes of Wrath," "12 Angry Men" and "On Golden Pond," Bridget made her film debut when she was five years old, appearing alongside her father, Peter Fonda, in the 1969 movie, "Easy Rider."

'80S ICON KRISTY MCNICHOL MAKES RARE APPEARANCE 25 YEARS AFTER LEAVING HOLLYWOOD

She had her breakthrough in 1989, when she starred in the film, "Scandal," and continued to prove herself in films such as "Single White Female," "Point of No Return," "It Could Happen to You" and "Jackie Brown."

Although she found big success as an actress, she slowed down in the late 1990s and into the 2000s. Her final movie role was in the 2001 TV movie, "After Amy," and her final time on-screen was in two episodes of the miniseries "Snow Queen," in 2002.

According to the Daily Mail, she told paparazzi in April 2023 that she had no plans to return to acting, noting, "It’s too nice being a civilian."

In addition to her grandfather and her father, Bridget also grew up with Academy Award-winning actress, Jane Fonda, who is her aunt. She explained that coming from an acting family, it was hard not to be compared to one another.

"At one time, there was nothing the press would have liked better than to set up a me vs Jane thing," she told The Guardian in 2000. "They were desperate for us to be bitter rivals. They'd also try to set me against my dad, to use me as a dart to throw at someone else."

After stepping away from Hollywood, Bridget married film composer and frontman for the band, Oingo Boingo, Danny Elfman, in 2003, and the two welcomed their son, Oliver, in 2005.

When speaking about her career in 1993, Bridget touched on her personal success and its connection to her famous last name.

"I wonder what kind of satisfaction I would have with where I am now if I wasn’t part of a family that has done such phenomenal work," she told Movieline.

"I wonder what it would feel like to know that you’ve made it completely under your own steam," she added. "I sometimes wonder if I would be more at peace if I could know I made it by myself, instead of always wondering how many times my name got me in the door."

item.title: Ohio State's College Football Playoff hopes take big hit with loss to Oregon, Jeremiah Smith shows frustration
item.description: Ohio State fell behind 38-14 after Oregon rattled off 38 unanswered points, raising very serious questions about the Buckeyes' playoff hopes.
item.content:encoded:
After being the No. 1 team in the preseason, Ohio State is proving why the games aren't played on paper.

The Buckeyes, 12th in the College Football Playoff rankings, were touchdown favorites against No. 23 Oregon but were dominated, 41-28, for their second loss in as many weeks.

It looked like all Buckeyes early, as they got out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter sans Julian Sayin, but someone lit a fire under Oregon's you-know-what, and they responded with 38 unanswered points.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The Buckeyes were two-and-a-half minutes away from going into the locker room with at least a 14-3 lead, but the Ducks faked a punt on 4th and 10, which apparently was the turning point. Five plays later, they found the end zone to cut the deficit to four, and then Luke Fahey threw an interception near midfield, which Oregon turned into a 17-14 lead right as the first half ended.

The bleeding did not stop, as momentum, and the ball, was all in Oregon's hands to start the second half. Dierre Hill Jr. took a 48-yard scamper to the house to go up two possessions, and the Buckeyes were stumped. After a three-and-out in their first drive of the second half, their next four drives resulted in turnovers on downs, all while Oregon managed to put up two more touchdowns to go up 38-14.

Jeremiah Smith had a 57-yard reception in garbage time to make his stats pretty (seven receptions for 133 yards), but let his emotions out on the field as he may have watched his Heisman chances slip away. He was held to just four catches through three quarters, three of them in the first half.

The Buckeyes had been the first team out of the first edition of the College Football Playoff rankings, and they unquestionably now face an uphill battle to play in the postseason.

DUKE'S BEATDOWN OF NC STATE INCLUDED A MUST-SEE MISSED FIELD GOAL RETURNED FOR A 109-YARD TOUCHDOWN

This defeat is off the heels of last week's 30-18 loss to USC as the second-ranked team in the AP poll. Thus, the team is 0-2 without Sayin, who many had in the Heisman conversation at the start of the season.

Nine Ducks caught at least one pass from Dylan Raiola (25-for-40, 257 yards, two touchdowns). Dakorien Moore and Brandon Smith combined for 10 catches for 108 yards, each with a score, while Hill scored twice on his 13 carries for 75 yards.

Now needing a lot of help, Ohio State will host Northwestern next week before a trip to Nebraska and then finishing the season hosting Michigan.

Oregon, meanwhile, is now hoping to backdoor its way into the playoff — they wrap up their campaign with Michigan, Michigan State and Washington the rest of the way.

item.title: Chili's sold nearly 30 million margaritas last year — and a $6 favorite stands out
item.description: Chili's sold nearly 30 million margaritas in 2025 and is expanding its drink lineup with premium pours and a Margarita of the Month Club.
item.content:encoded:
Chili's dominated restaurant chains in margarita sales in 2025 and is set to sell even more this year as the company finds new ways to keep its signature drink program fresh, according to a new report.

The chain sold nearly 30 million margaritas in 2025 and says that many customers come in specifically for the drinks, Nation's Restaurant News recently reported.

"Guests are coming to Chili’s for 'margs,'" Mary Ellen Scott, Chili's senior marketing director, told NRN. "It’s part of who we are and part of the experience."

CHILI'S GOES VIRAL AFTER ROASTING FAST-FOOD PRICES: 'WHY LET THEM PLAY YOU LIKE THIS?'

Frozen margaritas have been a Chili's menu staple since 1975, back when they cost just $1.50, and the chain has revamped the offering in recent years. Frozen drinks now account for 25% of its margarita sales.

Last year, Chili's launched a line of premium-liquor frozen margaritas and in February, it introduced a Margarita of the Month Club that allows customers to track how many of the drinks they bought and buy related merch, which is available for anyone to buy.

CHILI'S REVIVES ICONIC RED BOOTHS AND CLASSIC DESIGN IN NATIONWIDE RESTAURANT OVERHAUL

Customers can collect a digital badge for each month’s margarita and Scott says the "diehard" fans are eager to collect them all.

The club builds on the rotating Margarita of the Month program Chili's introduced in 2018, which draws customers in part for its low price of $6.

BABY BOOMERS CROWN THEIR FAVORITE CASUAL DINING CHAIN AS GEN Z CHOOSES A DIFFERENT WINNER

"It’s value, newness and fun," Scott told NRN. "It's always $6, the drink is changing every month, and we're always looking for ways to make the experience more fun, whether it's a candy or a swizzle."

Examples include October’s Witches Brew, a green drink made with Lunazul Blanco Tequila, blue Curaçao, and Monin Granny Smith Apple Syrup served with a broomstick "swizzle," or decorative stirrer.

November’s StrawEddy Marg combines the tequila with Deep Eddy Lemon Vodka, strawberry purée and house-made sour.

The premium-pour margs go for $10 to $12, which is still a steal when cocktails in many major cities are going for around $20.

The chain also has a full bar, but Scott says the margaritas remain its "flagship."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Chili's for comment.

Chili's margaritas made headlines last month for an unrelated safety incident in which North Carolina health officials said a cleaning chemical was mistakenly used to prepare drinks at a Forest City location, causing chemical burns to three customers.

Chili’s said guests and team members were injured and that it is investigating. The restaurant’s permit was briefly suspended, then reinstated.

item.title: Coach of NJ's top girls soccer team suspended for playoff game after champagne bottle celebration
item.description: Video shows New Jersey coach Karen Anderson popping a champagne bottle on school property after her 100th career win, triggering a suspension.
item.content:encoded:
A New Jersey girls' soccer coach has been suspended for a playoff game for celebrating a milestone victory with a champagne bottle.

Paul VI coach Karen Anderson was seen on video celebrating her 100th career win, a 2-0 win over Notre Dame in the South Jersey, Non-Public A quarterfinals, by what appeared to be popping the bottle on school property after the game.

Anderson told NJ.com that she did not drink from the bottle, which was bought and given by parents of members on the team. Anderson did not say whether the bottle had alcohol in it.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

The New Jersey State Interscholastic Athletic Association (NJSIAA) rulebook states that "[p]layers and coaches involved with alcohol/tobacco/illegal substances during or after the game at the game site or on school property, including chartered buses, shall be suspended from NJSIAA tournament play for one year and be denied any championship rights." So, perhaps the punishment is rather lenient.

Anderson told the outlet that she was "not surprised" that the video was coming to light "given our success."

"It’s really unfortunate that there are people out there looking for an opportunity to ruin all the hard work that I’ve put into this program," she said of the video, which has since been deleted from social media.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

"There sure are a lot of people that would look for a target to take an opportunity. It’s really unfortunate that somebody will find that one opportunity to jump on and try to take down everything that you have put into this."

"While Coach Anderson did not consume the contents of the bottle, Paul VI does not condone this behavior and recognizes the importance of upholding the standards of conduct expected of our coaches," Paul VI said Friday in a statement to the outlet.

Paul VI's girls' soccer team is the top-ranked team in the state and is two wins away from clinching its third-consecutive Non-Public A state championship.

item.title: Ex-police officer accused of stabbing NYC jogger to death appears emotionless in new photos
item.description: Sayed Mohassib was seen led away in handcuffs after being charged with second-degree murder in the stabbing death of Brooklyn jogger Katie Suarez.
item.content:encoded:
An ex-NYPD police officer accused of murdering a Brooklyn jogger was seen being out of the 62nd Precinct police station in handcuffs on Saturday.

Sayed Mohassib has been charged with second-degree murder in the stabbing Oct. 30 death of Katie Suarez at the Shore Parkway Greenway. 

He is also charged with physical evidence and criminal possession of a weapon.

Mohassib, who wore a red Van Dutch jacket, black top and jeans, showed little emotion as he was escorted by police.

NYC WOMAN CRITICALLY INJURED AFTER BEING STABBED MULTIPLE TIMES WHILE JOGGING ALONG BROOKLYN WATERFRONT

He told police that he woke up covered in blood with no memory of the attack, adding that he threw the knife in the garbage, according to the New York Post.

Suarez, 28, was running along a waterfront path around 8 p.m. when she was stabbed in her neck. 

She had been on the phone with her parents before the attack and when they got cut off, they went looking for her along the path where they found her in critical condition.

She died of her injuries at the hospital. 

COPS RETURN TO NEW JERSEY MOTHER'S HOME MONTHS AFTER SHE WAS FOUND STABBED AND HUSBAND CALLED 911

Mohassib briefly served with the NYPD before he left for the Marines, where he was deemed unfit for service, the Post reported.

The 27-year-old was most recently working as a public school aide. 

The New York City Department of Education told FOX 5 that Mohassib has been suspended and will be fired depending on a conviction.

"We are supporting the NYPD in their investigation however is needed," the department said.

Police have not released a motive or said if Mohassib had any relationship to Suarez.

item.title: College football fans and media rip SEC refs over controversial forward fumble call in Texas-Missouri game
item.description: Arch Manning's apparent incomplete pass was ruled a fumble, giving the Texas Longhorns a crucial first down that sparked a 21-0 run vs. Missouri.
item.content:encoded:
Apparently, you can throw an incomplete pass beyond the line of scrimmage and recover the ball for a first down in college football if you’re Arch Manning and the Texas Longhorns.

During Saturday's Texas-Missouri showdown, a matchup with massive College Football Playoff implications, the Longhorns were trailing 20-13 late in the third quarter when Manning dropped back on 3rd-and-10, appearing to throw an incomplete forward pass while getting hit. To the nation watching, it looked like Manning's arm was clearly moving forward before he lost control of the ball, but the officials apparently saw something the rest of America didn't.

ARCH MANNING, TEXAS ESCAPE MISSOURI AFTER WILD OFFICIATING CONTROVERSY SENDS SEC SHOWDOWN INTO CHAOS

One SEC sideline official called it an incomplete pass, while another allowed the play to continue, which isn’t too uncommon during a bang-bang play like this. Ultimately, the crew let the play stand and ruled it a forward fumble, allowing Texas receiver Emmett Mosley V to recover the ball 14 yards downfield for a first down.

During the review of the play, ABC/ESPN play-by-play announcer Joe Tessitore said astonishingly, "Are they saying this is not a forward pass and instead, a fumble?!"

Color commentator Jesse Palmer was also shocked.

Worst of all: The officials reviewed the play and somehow still decided it was a fumble. Three plays later, Texas scored the game-tying touchdown.

This obviously caused the college football world to melt down.

REFS' CRUCIAL NO CALL LOOMS LARGE OVER GEORGIA'S VICTORY OVER ALABAMA

One X user said they were "Questioning the integrity of this officiating crew."

Former referee, now rules analyst Terry McAulay said, "This is clearly and obviously an incomplete pass. He loses control after the hand moves forward."

Former Missouri and NFL quarterback, Chase Daniel was irate. "This is the most ridiculous call I’ve ever seen….you have the rules analyst and Jesse Palmer on the broadcast completely flabbergasted."

Outkick College Football Reporter Trey Wallace said, "This was called an Arch Manning fumble, and Texas picked up the 3rd down with a 12-yard gain. What the heck is happening at Missouri."

Former Missouri wide receiver T.J. Moe felt similarly saying, "This call knocked Mizzou out of playoff contention. Absolutely ridiculous. In what world is this not a forward pass?"

On3 personality David Pollack stated, "That was the craziest fumble forward I have ever seen for Texas."

Former NFL player Breiden Fehoko posted, "Real rigging going on Texas/Missouri game. Real talk this is so nasty."

FROM PHANTOM PASS INTERFERENCE TO IGNORED FACEMASK CALLS, NFL OFFICIATING FAILURES DEFINED WEEK 3

Many college football fans shared similar sentiments, calling it "rigged" and that the SEC was favoring Manning and the Longhorns for "ratings" and more accusations.

Just pencil this in as yet another officiating scandal that will continue to make fans and the media alike question the integrity of the game.

After the game, Missouri head coach Eli Drinkwitz wasn't particularly interested in donating his paycheck to the SEC by criticizing the officials, suggesting he'd be fined if he said what he really thought.

Texas ultimately scored 21 unanswered points to win 34-20, but the controversial call left Missouri fans wondering whether they had just witnessed a football game or a creative interpretation of the rulebook.

item.title: Rob Gronkowski's Patriots Hall of Fame celebration takes awkward turn with teammate's story about adult toys
item.description: Niko Koutouvides told an awkward story about Jenna Jameson adult toys and Aaron Hernandez at Rob Gronkowski's New England Patriots Hall of Fame ceremony.
item.content:encoded:
It's safe to say that former New England Patriots linebacker Niko Koutouvides won't be getting another speaking invitation from the team anytime soon.

Rob Gronkowski's induction into the New England Patriots Hall of Fame took an awkward turn on Saturday outside Gillette Stadium. Koutouvides recalled a story about how Gronkowski brought adult toys to training camp in 2011 and discussed them with Aaron Hernandez. The story didn't sit well with social media users.

"I'm going to ask all children here, whatever you hear, do not ask any questions after this, OK?" Koutouvides said to begin his story.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

When you have to tell children not to ask questions about what you are about to say, you probably shouldn't say it at all. But alas, Koutouvides plowed ahead.

"So Rob goes, 'I just got the Jenna Jameson adult toy', and for those who don't know, Jenna Jameson, she was like an Oscar-winning actress, OK. 'And this thing was awful, I got ripped off,'" Koutouvides said.

Jameson is an adult film actress, and Gronkowski put his head in his hands, appearing uncomfortable as Koutouvides started telling the story.

"So hold on, it gets a lot better than this guys. So then Aaron (Hernandez) rebuttals, 'Oh, I got a whole package in college,' and started to go through the description of each procedure you needed to take in order to be successful," Koutouvides continued.

"And it included microwaves and oils and all types of stuff. So I'm going into my eighth year in the league, they're just getting off their two phenomenal rookie seasons, they're going into Year Two. Remember, this is his phenomenal second year."

Koutouvides questioned why Gronkowski had brought the adult toy to training camp, where players would spend two and a half weeks.

"And I'm like, 'do I interject in this conversation?' and I just couldn't stay out of it. And I raised my hand and said 'can I communicate something with the two of you? Why are we talking about something that's prosthetic, right? Outside that door when we get out in two and a half weeks, is everything we want outside that door!'"

"And they both look at me and they go 'you've got a good explanation Niko but, more importantly, those two and a half weeks feel like three and a half years. And I said 'we're gonna have a great experience, the three of us', and the rest is history from there."

Gronkowski quickly made sure Koutouvides' speech was history once he concluded.

"Thank you very much, you're done," Gronkowski said.

Social media took issue with Koutouvides' story.

"A player that nobody knows goes up there and talks about Aaron Hernandez and an adult film star while being completely disjointed in telling an uninteresting story. Why was he speaking?" one user wrote on X.

Another fan called it "horrendous," while other fans questioned why Koutouvides was even speaking.

"2 things….what was that speech….and why was Koutivides there?" One fan wrote on X.

"Fun fact - not many people even knew who he was," another user wrote on X.

The best thing about Koutouvides' story? It's over.

item.title: Brooks Nader turns heads in sheer dress at CFDA Fashion Awards
item.description: Brooks Nader turned heads at the CFDA Fashion Awards in a sheer black-and-white metallic hooded dress ahead of her upcoming "Baywatch" reboot.
item.content:encoded:
Brooks Nader left little to the imagination when she walked the red carpet in a sheer dress on Monday.

The 29-year-old actress and model stunned when she posed for photos at the CFDA Fashion Awards in a sheer black-and-white metallic dress with a halter neckline and an attached hood.

Her black underwear was visible beneath the dress, which she paired with dark red nail polish, two rings, small hoop earrings and a pair of open-toed black high-heeled shoes.

She styled her hair in an updo which was mainly kept hidden beneath the hood of the dress, keeping one strand out to frame her face. Her makeup look was natural, with nude lipstick and winged eyeliner.

item.title: Duke's beatdown of NC State included a must-see missed field goal returned for a 109-yard touchdown
item.description: The Duke Blue Devils returned a missed NC State field goal 109 yards for a touchdown at Carter-Finley Stadium, turning a bad half into a nightmare.
item.content:encoded:
Not a whole lot has gone the NC State Wolfpack's way this season, and that was never more evident than after what the Duke Blue Devils did to them on Saturday afternoon in Raleigh.

The Wolfpack welcomed their in-state rivals to Carter-Finley Stadium amid a rough season that saw them enter the game at 4-4, just weeks removed from a coaching change.

Unfortunately, this one did not go their way, and the biggest bad bounce had to come at the very end of the first half, with NC State trailing 24-3.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION RUSSELL WILSON REPORTEDLY IN THE MIX FOR NC STATE HEAD-COACHING JOB

Interim head coach Todd Goebbel sent out his kicking team with two seconds on the clock, hoping that kicker Kanoah Vinesett could at least hit a 50-yard field goal to end the half on a semi-high note.

That did not happen. Vinesett didn't quite give it enough leg to get it the full 50 yards, and that worked out nicely for Duke as safety Andrew Pellicciotta was waiting in the end zone.

He hauled in the kick and took off 109 yards for a touchdown.

VANDERBILT PULLED OFF THE MOST IMPROBABLE LAST-SECOND VICTORY YOU'LL EVER SEE IN COLLEGE FOOTBALL

That was so shocking; whoever was manning the CW's scorebug thought the kick was as good as gold and hung three points on the board.

We don't see field goals returned for touchdowns nearly enough. It's easily one of the most exciting plays in football. The CFL got this right by having the goal posts at the front of the endzone (which also seems wildly unsafe, but at least they get more missed field goals returned for touchdowns).

The only folks who didn't enjoy that, however, were NC State fans.

That play flipped what should've been a 24-6 game at the half to one that was 31-3.

And unfortunately, it didn’t get any better as the Blue Devils tacked on another 10 points to win this one, 41-3.

item.title: Simple bedtime change may help some individuals lose weight, study finds
item.description: An NYU clinical trial found that moving bedtime just one hour earlier led to weight loss in prediabetes patients, even without longer sleep.
item.content:encoded:
Falling asleep earlier was linked to greater weight loss in adults with prediabetes, according to new research.

An analysis of data from a randomized trial led by the NYU Rory Meyers College of Nursing found that each hour earlier participants fell asleep was associated with roughly 1. 3 pounds of weight loss over eight weeks, although the finding does not prove that moving bedtime earlier causes weight loss.

"When we fall asleep — not just how much we sleep — seems to be an important and overlooked factor for weight loss and metabolic health," Susan Kohl Malone, an assistant professor at the nursing college and the study's lead author, said in a press release.

POPULAR WEIGHT-LOSS DRUGS MAY PREVENT PREDIABETES FROM TURNING INTO DIABETES

The investigation, published in the journal Nursing Research, evaluated 196 adults diagnosed with prediabetes who routinely logged fewer than 6.5 hours of sleep nightly. Half the group took part in an eight-week lifestyle education course on diet, exercise and stress.

The other half received the same training alongside behavioral coaching meant to get them to go to bed earlier in gradual phases.

DIETITIAN REVEALS SIMPLE EATING STRATEGY FOR BETTER SLEEP — AND ONE HABIT TO AVOID

Researchers tracked participants’ blood sugar, sleep and activity using sensors, sleep logs and wrist-worn monitors.

Neither group showed significant improvements in blood sugar. Both groups lost weight, but those receiving sleep coaching did not lose significantly more than those receiving lifestyle education alone.

"While we expected that extending sleep would improve glucose levels and weight loss in adults with prediabetes who sleep for shorter periods, this wasn't the case in our study," Malone said.

Participants who received sleep coaching did report better sleep quality and less daytime drowsiness, and they gradually began going to bed earlier.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR HEALTH NEWSLETTER

In a separate analysis across both groups, participants who shifted their sleep earlier tended to lose more weight.

The researchers suggested the body’s internal clock may help explain the findings. Staying up late can increase exposure to artificial light, which may activate the body’s stress response and affect hormones that regulate hunger.

Remaining awake late also coincides with the hours when human insulin sensitivity is at its lowest.

"In contrast, falling asleep earlier may limit late-night eating and better align food intake with the body's optimal metabolic window," Malone noted.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE HEALTH STORIES

The trial ran for only eight weeks, which means it's unclear whether participants could maintain earlier bedtimes or sustain weight loss over the long term.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

While participants wore wrist monitors, key sleep metrics like rest quality and daytime drowsiness relied heavily on self-reported logs.

The findings also show an association across the study group rather than proven cause and effect.

Participants receiving sleep coaching fell asleep about 12 minutes earlier on average, according to Malone, which produced no measurable improvement in blood sugar levels.

The study received funding from the National Institute of Nursing Research, a division of the National Institutes of Health, and was conducted in collaboration with researchers from the University of Delaware.

item.title: Israeli president taps Netanyahu rival to form government as coalition battle looms
item.description: Gadi Eisenkot secured 67 Knesset endorsements over Benjamin Netanyahu, but deep coalition divisions over Arab parties and conscription cloud his path.
item.content:encoded:
Israeli President Isaac Herzog announced Saturday that he has chosen opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot to form the country's next government, handing Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's chief rival the first opportunity to build a coalition following an inconclusive national election.

Herzog announced his decision on Nov. 7, but the formal presentation of the mandate is scheduled for Sunday, November 8, at 5 p.m. Israeli time. Eisenkot will then have 28 days to assemble a government, with a possible 14-day extension.

The decision could mark a significant step toward ending Netanyahu’s tenure, but it would also launch a difficult round of coalition negotiations, with deep disagreements among parties seeking to replace him.

NETANYAHU DEFIES EXIT POLLS AS VOTE SHIFTS IN HIS FAVOR, BUT MAJORITY REMAINS ELUSIVE

Following two days of consultations with Israel’s newly elected parliament, Herzog announced Thursday that factions representing 67 of the Knesset’s 120 members had recommended Eisenkot, chairman of the Yashar party, to form the next government. Netanyahu received the backing of 46 lawmakers, while seven members of the ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism party declined to endorse either candidate.

"The results of the consultations may appear clear," Herzog said in his Nov. 5 statement, but cautioned that competing political demands and vetoes have left the prospects for forming a government uncertain.

The challenge facing Eisenkot is that the 67 endorsements do not translate into a 67-seat governing coalition.

In the October 27 election, Netanyahu’s Likud emerged as the largest single party with 27 seats, while his wider political bloc won 53. The four-party alliance seeking to replace him secured just 48 seats.

The remaining endorsements for Eisenkot came from two Arab-led parties, the Joint List and Ra’am, which together hold 19 seats. Although both recommended Eisenkot to the president, their support presents a dilemma for some of his prospective coalition partners, who have ruled out depending on Arab parties to establish a government.

NETANYAHU GAINS OVERNIGHT AS ISRAEL ELECTION HEADS TOWARD POLITICAL DEADLOCK

In a lengthy statement Friday, Eisenkot outlined his plan to establish what he called a National Emergency Government, initially based on the four parties committed to replacing Netanyahu, while leaving the door open for additional parties and lawmakers to join.

"Israel is facing a genuine, tangible and dangerous national emergency," Eisenkot said. He accused the outgoing government of threatening Israeli democracy and warned that continued political instability could deepen the country's security and diplomatic challenges.

Eisenkot said negotiations with his political partners had already produced significant progress and that further talks were underway.

His proposed government would be based on four founding principles: recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; acceptance of the values of Israel’s Declaration of Independence; universal military, national or civilian service; and recognition of Hamas as a terrorist organization, alongside a commitment to dismantle its military and governing capabilities.

ISRAEL HEADS INTO DEEPLY DIVIDED ELECTION AS OCT. 7 RECKONING LOOMS: WHAT TO KNOW

Eisenkot said he would invite lawmakers from across the political spectrum to join his government if they accepted those principles.

But even within the bloc seeking to replace Netanyahu, disagreements remain over how to secure the parliamentary support needed to govern.

One potentially significant development came Friday when Avigdor Lieberman, leader of the secular nationalist Yisrael Beitenu party, signaled a willingness to compromise on military conscription for ultra-Orthodox Jews, reversing a position that had long prevented political cooperation with religious parties.

In a statement posted on X, Lieberman argued that preventing another election and ending Netanyahu’s time in office would require difficult political compromises.

He identified three conditions: ending the Netanyahu era, avoiding another election and refusing to establish a government dependent on the abstention of the Joint List and Ra’am.

On other matters, including the contentious military draft law, Lieberman said political leaders must be prepared to compromise.

BENJAMIN NETANYAHU'S LEGACY AND POLITICAL FUTURE ON THE LINE IN ISRAEL'S OCT 27 ELECTION

The shift could open a path to negotiations with United Torah Judaism, whose seven lawmakers withheld their recommendation from Netanyahu despite the party’s long standing political alliance with him.

United Torah Judaism leader Yaakov Asher welcomed Lieberman's flexibility Friday, but said his party had not yet received a concrete proposal and that any agreement would require approval from its religious leadership.

The conscription dispute remains a major obstacle. Ultra-Orthodox parties have sought legal protections for yeshiva students who study religious texts rather than serve in the military, while Eisenkot and several of his partners campaigned on expanding the obligation to serve.

Even bringing United Torah Judaism into the four-party opposition bloc would leave Eisenkot short of the 61 seats needed for an outright parliamentary majority. The religious Shas party, which holds six seats, recommended Netanyahu to Herzog.

A different possibility would be a minority government established with the help of abstentions from parties outside the coalition, an option discussed by Eisenkot’s allies but explicitly rejected by Lieberman if it depends on the Arab factions.

The disagreement exposes the central difficulty facing Eisenkot: although a majority of lawmakers recommended that he receive the first opportunity to form a government, they have not agreed on how such a government should be constituted.

Meanwhile, Netanyahu remains caretaker prime minister as the political negotiations continue.

The prime minister has also challenged aspects of the election results amid an investigation into suspected voting irregularities. However, Israel’s Central Elections Committee said the integrity of the election had not been compromised, according to Reuters on November 5.

For Eisenkot, receiving the presidential mandate would be an important political milestone. But turning his broad parliamentary endorsement into a functioning government will require agreements among parties divided over some of Israel’s most contentious domestic issues, particularly military service and cooperation with Arab lawmakers.

Failure to bridge those divisions could leave Israel facing further political deadlock — and potentially another election.

item.title: Dustin Hoffman had a 'terrible experience' making Hollywood classic 'The Graduate'
item.description: Dustin Hoffman reveals in a new essay that he felt "unworthy" and feared being fired every day while filming "The Graduate" with Mike Nichols.
item.content:encoded:
Dustin Hoffman is opening up about the "terrible experience" he had while filming "The Graduate," a film he said "exacerbated all my insecurities from the start."

In a recent essay written for The New Yorker, the 89-year-old actor reflected on his experience making the film, which earned him his first Academy Award nomination and a BAFTA Award win, noting he "felt immediately uncomfortable" and "unworthy" on set.

"Here I was, playing a starring role in a movie by Mike Nichols, who was the director of the moment, but I felt like I had no right to be there," he wrote. "It was a terrible experience making the movie that changed my life."

He went on to explain that a lot of his time on set was spent wondering if director, Nichols, "was angry at me," because he was either "doing something wrong" or had finally noticed what Hoffman and "everybody else already knew, that he had miscast the lead in his film."

JOHN GOODMAN ADMITS HE FELT 'FRIGHTENED' AFTER THE SUDDEN FAME HE EXPERIENCED FROM 'ROSEANNE'

The "Rain Man" star felt he was wrong for the part from the start, admitting he "didn't even want to try out for the part," saying he thought "it was obvious" to him after reading the novel the film is based on "that I was all wrong for Benjamin."

"A track star and straight-A student, the head of the debate team—this was an affluent, all-American kid, whose surname was ‘Braddock,’" he said. "Why would you cast a person who looks as ethnic as I do to play the ultimate Wasp? It made absolutely no sense." 

Part of what made the experience so bad for Hoffman was his relationship with the director, who he said was "irritable with everyone," and was "frequently sour" on set.

The director's attitude often led to Hoffman feel "that I was about to be fired," as the actor found himself "thinking, I have no f- - -ing idea what I'm doing," while filming some of the most well-known scenes in the movie.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

Hoffman also recalled feeling as if the director had a "certain sadism" that was directed mostly towards him.

"There was a scene in which Katharine Ross had to slap me, and he made us do twenty-seven takes. The scene has Benjamin run into Elaine’s room, soaking wet from the rain, to tell her that he’s had an affair with an older woman; within seconds, Elaine realizes the woman is her mother," he said. "Mike just kept telling Katharine to hit me, to hit me harder. Katharine worried she would hurt me, and I told her, ‘I’m O.K. Just don’t hit my ear.’ Unfortunately, she missed a few times. I was dizzy by the end of that day, and Mike didn’t even use the slap in the film."

The next day, Hoffman was scheduled to film a scene underwater, which left him with "blood trickling out of my ear," which later turned out to be a punctured eardrum.

"The Graduate" went on to become one of Hoffman's most well-known films. The movie follows Hoffman's character, Benjamin, a recent college graduate who is struggling to find direction post graduation and is seduced by an older housewife and friend of his parents.

Following its release in 1967, the film was nominated for seven Academy Awards, including best actor for Hoffman and best actress for Anne Bancroft, and ultimately earned Nichols a statue for best director.

item.title: Army student displays hilarious 'communism' sign ahead of game against Air Force
item.description: Army football leads the entire FBS with 342.5 rushing yards per game through eight games in 2026 while throwing just 85 passes all season long.
item.content:encoded:
Army is taking "boots on the ground" to another level, according to their fans.

Fox's Big Noon Kick-off visited West Point ahead of their matchup against rival Air Force Academy . One Army student had a sign that stood out above the rest, making Mark Ingram II take notice and chest bump him. The sign said, "The Forward Pass is Communist."

In case you weren't aware, Army football doesn't just favor running the football, the Black Knights practically treat the forward pass like it's anti-American. They essentially wage war against the forward pass. Army consistently ranks among the nation's leaders in rushing attempts and rushing yards while sitting near the bottom in passing volume.

WHO'S REALLY PLAYED THE BEST THUS FAR THROUGH THE FIRST HALF OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON?

Rather than airing it out, the Black Knights rely on quarterback keepers, fullback dives and option pitches to grind down opposing defenses, dominate time of possession and keep the clock moving. It's old-school, smash mouth football, which I'm sure gets the boomers to say, "Now this is the football I grew up with!"

Through eight games in 2026, Army leads the entire FBS in rushing yards per game (342.5), piling up 2,740 yards on 431 rushing attempts, an average of 53.9 carries per game. That's a whopping 6.4 yards per carry and 31 rushing touchdowns. Meanwhile, the passing game is practically nonexistent. Army ranks 137th out of 138 FBS teams in passing yards per game (69.1) , attempting just 85 passes all season — a measly 10.6 per game, the second-fewest in the country behind Air Force. The Black Knights have thrown for just four touchdowns compared to 31 on the ground, with nearly 83% of their offensive plays coming on rushing attempts.

A LIST OF THE BEST COLLEGE GAMEDAY SIGNS AT LSU DURING SHOW'S 500TH EPISODE

While most college programs are obsessed with throwing the ball all over the field, Army has a much simpler philosophy: Why throw the football when you can run it down your opponent's throat?

Army (5-3) hosts Air Force (6-2) on Saturday at Michie Stadium in West Point, New York, with kickoff scheduled for 7:30 p.m. ET. The matchup is part of the annual Commander-in-Chief's Trophy competition, with Army looking for its fourth consecutive victory over the Falcons in a battle featuring the nation's top two rushing offenses.

item.title: IIHF 'taking the necessary steps' to comply with Russia return ruling as Belarus ban remains
item.description: The IIHF says it disagrees with the CAS ruling but is taking steps to allow Russia in the World Junior Championships amid a multinational boycott.
item.content:encoded:
The International Ice Hockey Federation provided updates on Belarusian and Russian athletes in its upcoming world tournaments, including next month's World Junior Championships.

The IIHF announced Saturday that Belarus will not participate, but the federation is "taking the necessary steps required" to comply with the Court of Arbitration for Sport's (CAS) ruling to allow Russia to play.

"While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships, protect the organization’s financial stability and secure the long-term future of international ice hockey," the federation said in a statement. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

"The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues, including opening discussions with all affected MNAs, including the Russian Ice Hockey Federation, to identify a constructive way forward that serves the interests of global ice hockey."

The CAS ruled last week that Russian teams can compete in upcoming men's and women's world championships, overturning the International Ice Hockey Federation's (IIHF) decisions to exclude them from its competitions. The World Juniors will be the first tournament affected by the decision.

Hockey Canada and Prime Minister Mark Carney said last week that Russians would not be allowed to play in next month's World Juniors, which will take place in Alberta.

Russia did not compete in Olympic hockey earlier this year, the first since 2014 that had NHL players, nor was it included in the NHL's 4 Nations Face-Off. Russia invaded Ukraine on Feb. 24, 2022, four days after Olympic competition ended that year.

Vladimir Putin put out a statement through the state-run Russian outlet TASS calling out organizations that are preventing Russian athletes from competing for their country.

HOCKEY GREAT WAYNE GRETZKY DEFENDS RELATIONSHIP WITH PRESIDENT TRUMP AND SPEAKS ON RUSSIAN HOCKEY BAN

"Unfortunately, they have not honored the commitments they once made, and they continue to enforce restrictions against Russian sports that are not based on law, but are instead highly politicized," Putin said, via translation. "This constitutes a clear and gross violation of the law and of judicial rulings — and, by extension, a violation of the very institutions of democracy. That is precisely how this should be interpreted."

Sweden, Finland, the Czech Republic, Norway, Latvia and Denmark came out with statements signing up for a boycott of games against Russia as long as the war in Ukraine is ongoing. Germany, the host of the 2027 men's world championships, also suggested backing out if Russia was allowed to play.

STRAUSS, a workwear company that is a top sponsor of the world championships next year, threatened to walk away after Finland announced Monday it was rallying other nations to refuse to play Russia.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

If Russia makes the trip next month, it will be its first time playing in the World Juniors since 2021. It has not won gold since 2011.

item.title: Urgent travel alert as nationwide strike threatens widespread disruption and delays
item.description: Spain's 24-hour nationwide strike on Nov. 11 could disrupt flights, trains and Barcelona metro service as unions protest the housing crisis.
item.content:encoded:
Travelers heading to Spain this coming week are being urged to check flight and train plans ahead of a 24-hour nationwide strike.

Spain’s two largest unions, UGT and CCOO, have called a 24-hour nationwide strike for Nov. 11 over the housing crisis, The Independent reported. The U.S. Embassy says workers across sectors, including transportation and hospitality, have been called to participate.

Flights, trains and local transit could face disruptions, with demonstrations expected in major cities, though not all specific service interruptions have been confirmed.

AMERICANS WARNED OF VIOLENT PROTESTS AS MAJOR TOURIST DESTINATION FACES SHUTDOWN THREAT

Demonstrations including picket lines may also prompt last-minute closures, cancellations, roadblocks and an increased police presence, according to an alert from the U.S. Embassy & Consulate in Spain and Andorra. Shops, restaurants, museums and pharmacies may also close, according to the advisory.

"Demonstrations, both planned and spontaneous, will occur throughout the country," it read. "Even protests, demonstrations, and gatherings intended to be peaceful can escalate quickly or have the potential to turn violent."

FURIOUS CROWDS PROTEST SKY-HIGH HOUSING COSTS AND MASS TOURISM IN MAJOR CITY

Some details on local interruptions are already available, according to the government of Catalonia's website.

In Catalonia, public transportation — including Barcelona’s metro, buses and regional rail — is set to run at 25% of normal service during morning and evening peak periods: 6:30 to 9:30 a.m. and 4:30 to 9 p.m.

CRUISE PASSENGERS FACE BLOCKED ACCESS AS ANGRY PROTESTERS SET BARRICADES ON FIRE

The bus linking Barcelona and its airport is scheduled to operate at 50% of normal service. Outside the peak windows, no minimum service level has been set for passenger transportation, though that does not necessarily mean all service will stop.

Separately, Catalonia’s commuter and regional rail services will operate at 66% of normal service during peak hours and 33% the rest of the day on Nov. 10 and 12 amid the Renfe train-driver strikes.

ANGRY LOCALS BLOCK FAMOUS BEACH AS MASS TOURISM PROTESTS ESCALATE AT VACATION HOT SPOT

The strike’s effect on individual flights, trains and local services may vary. Travelers should check directly with their airline, train company and local transit operator for updates, and allow extra time to reach airports and stations.

The embassy also advises U.S. citizens to avoid demonstrations and crowds, monitor local news and follow instructions from police and local authorities.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

The walkout comes amid demonstrations over housing affordability. One of the major unions said its call seeks urgent action on the housing crisis, along with better wages and labor and social protections.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS

Recent demonstrations and labor actions across Spain in recent weeks have highlighted several other issues, including rising rents and short-term rentals, calls to restrict tourism in Mallorca and Ibiza, and potential pay cuts for Barcelona port workers, whose protest temporarily blocked access to cruise terminals.

TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ

Recent protests elsewhere in Europe have reflected varied local grievances, including housing costs, the cost of living and pressure on public services, according to reports, though they are not necessarily connected to Spain’s strike.

item.title: Melania Trump secures $7.2M for foster care scholarships at LSU ahead of Alabama showdown
item.description: Melania Trump unveiled a $7.2 million scholarship endowment at LSU for foster care youth before receiving a custom jersey and football tribute.
item.content:encoded:
BATON ROUGE, La. — First lady Melania Trump announced a $7.2 million scholarship endowment at Louisiana State University (LSU) on Saturday, delivering a message of hope to young Americans who have experienced foster care before receiving a special football tribute ahead of the Tigers' rivalry showdown against Alabama.

Trump wore a Dalma suede bomber jacket by Nour Hammour, paired with an Adam Lippes skirt and Manolo Blahnik BB pumps for the occasion, blending her signature polished style with a more relaxed look suited to a college football weekend.

The first lady's visit unfolded against a distinctly LSU backdrop, with purple-and-gold tailgating crowds lining the motorcade route and a massive American flag hanging above the stage inside Patrick F. Taylor Hall. 

LSU cheerleaders flanked Trump during her remarks, and the Tiger mascot presented her with both scholarship checks while wearing a signature "Be Best" T-shirt.

MELANIA TRUMP CHALLENGES CONGRESS TO MAKE HER FOSTER CARE EXECUTIVE ORDER PERMANENT LAW: 'THEIR BIRTHRIGHT'

There, university officials, donors and students gathered for an announcement supporting young Americans who have experienced foster care through Trump's "Fostering the Future" initiative.

"This achievement will give young people from foster care an anchor of stability, a strong educational foundation, and a chance to build a wonderful life," Trump told attendees.

The permanent endowment includes a $5 million commitment from MMR Group, led by LSU alumnus James B. "Pepper" Rutland, and an additional $2.2 million raised from 75 LSU Foundation donors.

LSU Foundation President and CEO Krista Raney said the contributions had brought the scholarship fund to "more than $7.2 million and growing."

LSU President Wade Rousse said the $5 million leadership gift is expected to generate approximately $200,000 annually, helping students cover tuition, fees, books and room and board.

ED ORGERON-LANE KIFFIN PAIRING ALREADY PAYING DIVIDENDS FOR LSU TIGERS DURING PIVOTAL RECRUITING WEEKEND

"At LSU, we believe talent is everywhere, but we understand that opportunity is not," Rousse said.

The university also embraced the occasion with several football-themed gifts for the first lady.

Trump received a custom purple-and-gold LSU jersey bearing the name "MELANIA" and the number 14, along with a Tigers helmet featuring her BE BEST Fostering the Future logo.

Former LSU coach Ed Orgeron, known to fans as Coach O, joined the presentation with a specially designed commemorative football created by Big Game USA, a company owned by LSU alumnus Chris Calandra.

The initiative extended beyond the ceremony, with special patches on LSU players' jerseys, helmet decals, cheerleader uniforms, mascot attire and commemorative fan towels, according to the White House.

COLLEGE FOOTBALL'S FIRST FULL SATURDAY IS HERE AND IT'S A CELEBRATION OF AMERICA AT ITS BEST

The celebration continued at Tiger Stadium, where the first lady's Fostering the Future initiative received a special on-field recognition during LSU's highly anticipated matchup against Alabama.

Students joined LSU's Mike the Tiger mascot and others on the field for a ceremonial check presentation highlighting the $7.2 million scholarship endowment. Trump also appeared on the stadium's massive Jumbotron as fans cheered and chants of "USA" echoed through the stadium.

The game-day atmosphere included a military flyover above Tiger Stadium, adding to the spectacle as thousands of fans gathered for the SEC rivalry.

The first lady's visit extended beyond the scholarship announcement, with LSU incorporating Fostering the Future branding into players' jerseys, helmets and other game-day elements. 

A special Melania Trump challenge coin was also designated for the game's opening coin toss, according to the White House.

The legendary LSU-Alabama rivalry even found its way into the scholarship announcement.

After Trump revealed that LSU has 14 Fostering the Future scholars compared with Alabama's nine, Raney offered a lighthearted observation.

"Mrs. Trump, what I heard you say is that LSU has 14 scholarship recipients and Alabama has nine," Raney said. "So I think that means we've already won the first point."

Trump told attendees that 26 universities nationwide are supporting 100 Fostering the Future scholars this semester.

"While most eyes will be on the athletes today, I encourage you to recognize LSU's Fostering the Future scholars, who are just as remarkable," she said.

Louisiana Gov. Jeff Landry, Louisiana first lady Sharon Landry and House Majority Leader Steve Scalise, R-La., were among those in attendance.

Trump also received a handcrafted wooden bowl made from a fallen limb of one of LSU's historic oak trees, a gift symbolizing the lasting impact of the scholarship initiative.

Fostering the Future, launched in 2021 as part of Trump's BE BEST initiative, seeks to expand educational opportunities for young people who have experienced foster care.

"A great education does more than prepare someone for work life," Trump said. "It gives something no one can ever take away."

She closed with an encouraging message to scholarship recipients.

"To the Fostering the Future scholars here today, and throughout America: I see you. I believe in you. And I will keep working to create new opportunities with you," she said.

item.title: JACKSON THOMPSON: Trump says he offered UFC CEO Dana White press secretary job
item.description: President Donald Trump proposed UFC CEO Dana White as White House press secretary in a Truth Social post, naming MMA fighters as assistants.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump said Saturday he had offered UFC CEO Dana White the White House press secretary job, proposing a team of mixed martial arts stars to help defend his administration against political opponents.

Shortly after Trump published his post, White shared a photo on his Instagram Story of himself standing at the White House press podium with the caption, "On to the next chapter." He also shared Trump’s Truth Social post announcing the offer.

The Nov. 7 Truth Social post paired the proposed offer with a roster of fighters and an image collage. It did not establish that White had accepted the position, and it was not immediately clear whether Trump intended the proposal seriously.

"We need these people to defend us against the Lunatic Left," Trump wrote.

DANA WHITE SAYS 'I DON'T GIVE A S---' IF TRUMP FRIENDSHIP COSTS HIM BUSINESS, 250TH EVENT WAS TRUMP'S IDEA

The president named Islam Makhachev, Khabib Nurmagomedov, Justin Gaethje, Daniel Cormier and Amanda Nunes as prospective assistants, while acknowledging that some were not American. He also listed "Kayla Harris," apparently referring to UFC fighter and two-time Olympic judo gold medalist Kayla Harrison.

"Dana, please take the job!" Trump added.

The post comes amid turnover in the White House’s senior ranks and weeks after the departure of Trump’s most recent press secretary.

Fox News Digital reported Oct. 16 that Katie Zacharia was leaving the position following her debut. Trump had announced her selection Oct. 9 to succeed Karoline Leavitt, who left in August. ABC News reported that Zacharia began work Oct. 12 and was transitioning out of the role that Friday.

Asked Oct. 23 about finding another press secretary, Trump told reporters, "No, nothing much. We’re in no rush."

Separately, the White House announced Friday that Stephen Miller would succeed Susie Wiles as chief of staff. That announcement confirmed a personnel change; Trump’s Saturday appeal to White left the proposed press secretary arrangement unresolved.

UFC'S DANA WHITE SAYS 'YOU'D BE SHOCKED' TO LEARN WHO ACTUALLY SUPPORTS TRUMP IN THE SHADOWS

White and Trump have a relationship stretching back decades, rooted partly in Trump’s support for UFC when the promotion was working to establish itself.

Trump hosted UFC events in Atlantic City as early as 2001, according to Sports Business Journal. White later became a prominent supporter of Trump’s presidential campaigns and spoke during his 2024 election-night victory celebration.

White also introduced Trump at the 2024 Republican National Convention in Milwaukee, describing their long friendship and praising Trump’s resilience.

Their relationship carried into Trump’s second term. The president attended UFC Freedom 250 on the White House South Lawn on June 14, 2026. Official White House photographs documented Trump and White walking through the building together to attend the event.

White has previously downplayed the prospect of entering politics himself.

"I have no personal political aspirations," he told Sports Business Journal in November 2024 when asked about a potential role in Trump’s incoming administration.

That statement preceded Saturday’s post by two years and does not establish White’s response to the latest proposal.

OutKick has reached out to the White House and UFC for comment.

item.title: Liberal podcasters apologize after laughing at joke about digging up Charlie Kirk's body
item.description: Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan laughed on the "I've Had It" podcast over a post referencing Charlie Kirk's death, sparking outrage.
item.content:encoded:
Podcasters Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan drew criticism from political commentators after laughing at a social media post about exhuming the body of conservative activist Charlie Kirk. The two issued an apology on Saturday. 

During Thursday's episode of Welch's "I've Had It" podcast, the two women laughed as they read social media reactions to Democrats' victories in the 2026 midterm elections. Several posts mocked conservative positions on issues including abortion, vaccines and LGBTQ+ policies.

"Somebody posted, ‘I don’t care if you celibate or abstinent. Grab the nearest person available and do your worst. Abortion’s on me,’" Welch said, reading from the social media posts.

STATE OF PLAY: BLUE WAVE SWEEPS DEMOCRATS INTO POWER, WITH KEY RACES STILL HANGING IN BALANCE

The pair continued to laugh as they read other social media reactions mocking Republicans following the party's midterm election losses.

"You can't even fathom the pronouns we're going to invent," Welch read while laughing. "You can't even pronounce them."

The podcast host praised the writers of the various posts, calling the jokesters "patriots" and insisting that "these people make me patriotic."

Welch further broke out into laughter while reading another post aloud: "We're digging up Charlie Kirk and doing it again."

'SNL' WEEKEND UPDATE ANCHOR CALLS REPUBLICANS SLURS, MOCKS CHARLIE KIRK IN STAND-UP SPECIAL

On Saturday, the two hosts apologized via a post on Instagram.

"On Thursday’s show, we laughed at a joke about Charlie Kirk. It was an insensitive joke, and we should not have laughed. We regret it, and we apologize," the statement read. "Whatever our political differences, there is nothing funny about gun violence. We’ve long supported common-sense gun safety reform." 

"To that end, we’ve made a donation to Everytown for Gun Safety, the largest gun violence prevention organization in America," the statement continued. "We’ll keep using our platforms to fight for the safety of all Americans."

During Thursday's episode, after laughing at the post, the hosts said, "No comment," before asserting without presenting evidence that Tyler Robinson, the man accused of killing Kirk, supported President Donald Trump.

DEMOCRATIC STUDENT GROUP TO PROTEST CHARLIE KIRK MEMORIAL AT CAMPUS WHERE HE WAS KILLED

"Other than he was shot by somebody that was super MAGA," Sullivan said.

"He was shot by a MAGA person," Welch said, adding, "White person, White MAGA family."

REMEMBERING CHARLIE KIRK: TURNING POINT USA'S ANDREW KOLVET REFLECTS ON CONSERVATIVE GROUP'S CHALLENGING YEAR

While Robinson and his family lived in Utah’s Washington County, a deep red county where 75% of residents voted to send President Donald Trump back to the White House, Fox News Digital previously reported that Utah Voter Registration records showed that Robinson is unaffiliated with a political party and did not vote in the past two general elections.

Several commentators criticized the hosts' remarks on social media.

PETE DAVIDSON SPARKS BACKLASH AFTER EXPLICIT JOKE ABOUT SLAIN CHARLIE KIRK DURING NETFLIX ROAST

"In all of their hatred and blood thirst, these ghouls seriously consider themselves morally superior to you," conservative activist Riley Gaines said in an X post.

"They will celebrate your death, laugh uncontrollably, and still be fully convinced they're the 'good guys,'" influencer Collin Rugg posted.

Media Research Center President David Bozell also criticized the hosts, telling Fox News Digital, "If Madison Ave. would stop sponsoring gutter trash, gutter trash would go out of business."

Democratic strategist Kaivan Shroff also criticized Welch and Sullivan's remarks.

BOBBY BURACK: ONLINE HATE IS WINNING, FROM PAT MCAFEE TO EVERYDAY AMERICANS AND YOUNG CHILDREN

"As a Democrat, it is frustrating to watch Jennifer Welch and Angie Sullivan get treated like voices for the Democratic Party when so much of their own brand is railing against Democrats," Shroff told Fox News Digital. "Have either of them persuaded a single person to vote for a Democrat?"

"Then, after Democrats just delivered historic wins and a massive blue wave, they say something this offensive and irresponsible and suddenly the story is about them instead," he added. "They are not helping Democrats. They are hijacking the attention Democrats actually earned at the ballot box."

Welch and Sullivan did not immediately respond to Fox News Digital’s request for comment.

Fox News Digital's Deirdre Heavey contributed to this report.

item.content:encoded:

item.title: Sami Zayn leaves WWE Crown Jewel with more than just a championship after loss to Roman Reigns
item.description: Roman Reigns declared Sami Zayn "an Uso" after their WWE Crown Jewel Championship match in an emotional moment that stunned the Riyadh crowd.
item.content:encoded:
Sami Zayn lost to Roman Reigns in the main event on Saturday, but came away with something that likely meant more to him than the WWE Crown Jewel Championship. Respect.

It’s all Zayn ever really wanted from his former Bloodline brother. It’s what he’s wanted from the WWE Universe and the rest of the locker room on SmackDown. He’s said for months he didn’t feel like he was getting the respect he’s earned through his years of hard work in the ring. He said he didn’t get it when he became the undisputed WWE champion the first time or the second time.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK PRO WRESTLING COVERAGE

Reigns left no doubt in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia. Zayn demanded that Reigns shake his hand in the ring. He asserted that he deserved that much. Reigns countered with something else. A passionate hug that will stand the test of time and adds another element to their story that goes back a few years to when Zayn was an "honorary Uce" in The Bloodline.

"You’re not honorary. You’re an Uso," Reigns declared.

The emotional moment capped an incredible match.

Zayn walked into what felt like a home game. He captured the Undisputed WWE Championship for the first time earlier this year at Night of Champions when the premium live event was held in Saudi Arabia. Zayn, who is of Syrian descent, made it an unbelievable moment.

The crowd was behind Zayn from the get-go and tried his best to get into the mind of Reigns throughout the match. Reigns was above all the nonsense. He hit Zayn with one more spear and pinned him for the victory.

For Reigns, another accolade has been added to his already impressive WWE resume.

Reigns is a seven-time world champion. He’s won the Intercontinental, United States and Tag Team Championship and has picked up victories in the Royal Rumble twice, including earlier this year. Now, he can also add the Crown Jewel Championship and the Crown Jewel ring to his list of accomplishments.

Hungry competitors await Reigns when he returns to the U.S. Zayn may have been the annoying gnat that flew around him who could be squashed. It doesn’t appear that the 946 is going to be as easy to take care of.

Cruz Montana joined the group this past week on "Monday Night Raw." The Royce Keys-led faction have been one of the only groups to get the better of Reigns and The Bloodline.
